evidence.effect: Market intraday momentum (r_ROD -> r_LH), soybean oil's own row
evidence.rule: r_LH = a + b*r_ROD; r_ROD = return from prior close to 30 min before close, r_LH = last half-hour return (BO session 08:30-13:20 CT)
evidence.hold: last 30 min of the day session
evidence.conversion: BO slope 0.03 (x100) with t 0.08: no effect to size. 1 ZL tick = 0.01 c/lb = $6. bp per tick = 100/P (P in c/lb). Public level used: IMF global soybean-oil price via FRED PSOILUSDM, mean 39.52 c/lb over 2010-07..2019-04 (2.53 bp/tick) and 50.75 c/lb over 2019-05..2024-02 (1.97 bp/tick); a proxy, not the CBOT ZL price. D8 RT wall 2.675 ticks ($16.05) = 6.8 bp at 39.5 c/lb, 5.3 bp at 50.75 c/lb; 1.5x = 4.01 ticks ($24.08).
evidence.sample: BO (CBOT soybean oil, Tickdata), 1982-07-06..2020-05-01, 9458 obs, 1-min bars
evidence.decay_evidence: none needed: in-sample null; R2 -0.01%, R2_OOS -0.06%. Pooled 'Softs' group (12 ags incl. BO) b_ROD 0.65 (t 2.16), R2_OOS -0.01%.
evidence.source: Baltussen, Da, Lammers, Martens (2021), JFE 142, 377-403, Table B3 Panel B (on-disk publisher copy; NQ reader owns the full read)
evidence.quote_location: Table B3 Panel B, row BO (columns: bONFH, R2, R2OOS, bTONFH, bM, bSLH, R2, R2OOS, bROD, R2, R2OOS; slopes and R2 x100); caption: 'Panel B: Newey and West (1986) robust t-statistics'; Softs row in Panel A: '| Softs | 0.25 (0.70) | ... | 0.65** (2.16) | 0.04 | -0.01 |'; sample row: '| Soybean oil futures | BO | 1982-07-06 | 2020-05-01 | 9458 | 08:30-13:20 | Softs |'

evidence.effect: Intraday cointegration of the soybean crush (ZS, ZL, ZM) in the day session; stronger on USDA days
evidence.rule: none (econometric; no trading rule). Cointegration of 1-min ZS/ZL/ZM prices, 08:30-13:20 CT session vs 19:00-07:45 session
evidence.sample: ZS, ZL, ZM CME market-by-order data, all of 2015 (243 trading days), 1-min snapshots
evidence.decay_evidence: one year only; no out-of-sample or post-publication test
evidence.source: Zhou, Bagnarosa, Gohin, Pennings, Debie (2023), 'Microstructure and high frequency price discovery in the soybean complex', J. Commodity Markets 30, 100314 (CC BY)
evidence.quote: A high level of cointegration is indeed observed during session 2 trading hours, which fades away during session 1. Another interesting result is the stronger intraday cointegration observed on average on USDA announcement days, although the number of observations available is limited.
evidence.quote_location: Section 5.1, PDF p. 10; sample: 'The high-frequency data used in this study covers the total trading activity of 2015, amounting to 243 trading days.' (Section 4, PDF p. 8)

evidence.effect: Biofuel-policy events (EPA RVO announcements, CARB quarterly reports, Reuters 'sources' leaks) raise soybean oil ABSOLUTE daily returns on the event day and the day after
evidence.rule: none tradable: unsigned (absolute) close-to-close returns; EPA events and leaks are unscheduled (no calendar known in advance); CARB reports fall on the last day of each quarter
evidence.conversion: 0.59% and 0.62% are increases in |return|, not signed returns; no direction, so no per-trade gross. 1 ZL tick = 0.01 c/lb = $6. bp per tick = 100/P (P in c/lb). Public level used: IMF global soybean-oil price via FRED PSOILUSDM, mean 39.52 c/lb over 2010-07..2019-04 (2.53 bp/tick) and 50.75 c/lb over 2019-05..2024-02 (1.97 bp/tick); a proxy, not the CBOT ZL price. D8 RT wall 2.675 ticks ($16.05) = 6.8 bp at 39.5 c/lb, 5.3 bp at 50.75 c/lb; 1.5x = 4.01 ticks ($24.08).
evidence.sample: Daily nearby/first-deferred futures from Bloomberg, 2019..2025-02 (1,034 trading days); 36 events 2021-2025
evidence.decay_evidence: none; sample is 2021-2025 only (no backward-window evidence; RD/biofuel demand regime)
evidence.source: Avileis and Swanson (2025), 'Drivers of Commodity Volatility in the Biofuel Era', NCCC-134 proceedings
evidence.quote: We calculate absolute returns for all commodities and the crush as the difference between market open (i.e., market close of the previous trading day) and market close for a single day.
evidence.quote_location: Section 3 Data, p. 10-11 (the PDF's ligature for 'difference' is garbled in pdftotext as 'di!erence'); abstract: 'soybean oil futures returns increase significantly on announcement days (0.59%) and continue rising the following day (0.62%)'; Section 5.1 p. 18: 'absolute returns cumulative increase by 1.21% on a two-day window'

evidence.effect: Crush-spread mean reversion driven by intraday deviations from the USDA-implied processing relationship; strategies profitable after costs
evidence.rule: not available (abstract only); legs ZS, ZM, ZL
evidence.source: Abdoh and Chitavi (2025), 'Mean reversion of the soybean crush spread: A new model and trading strategies', Int. Review of Economics & Finance 101 (paywalled; no preprint found)
evidence.quote: Our simulations demonstrate that trading strategies based on these findings would have been profitable, even after accounting for transaction costs. This analysis is based on 8650 trading days from September 1990 to May 2021.

evidence.effect: USDA reports and Dalian (DCE) soybean oil futures: minute volatility and volume react at the DCE open, price reactions fade within minutes; reduced impact on DCE soybean oil in the trade-war period
evidence.rule: none (volatility/volume event study; DCE, not CBOT ZL)
evidence.sample: DCE soybean no.1, no.2, soybean oil, soybean meal, 2011-01..2021-04, minute data
evidence.decay_evidence: trade-war period: reduced impact on DCE soybean oil
evidence.source: Hu and Mallory (2022 NCCC-134; published J. Futures Markets 45(11), 2025)
evidence.quote: On average, price reactions dissipate within a few minutes, while increased trading volume can last up to an hour. ... During the trade war period, USDA reports had reduced impact on soybean no. 1 and soybean oil futures but remained influential on soybean no. 2 and soybean meal futures.
evidence.quote_location: JFM 2025 abstract (IDEAS record, saved ideas_hu_mallory_jfm2025.html); NCCC full text saved and read for scope only (p. 2-3: 'impacts and becomes fully incorporated into soybean no.1, soybean no. 2, soybean oil, and soybean meal futures contracts on the DCE')

evidence.effect: Intraday momentum/reversal on 31 Chinese commodity futures (minute data, includes the DCE soybean-oil contract per 'complete' dataset): intraday strategies do not cover costs
evidence.sample: 31 Chinese commodities, minute bars (years not in abstract)
evidence.source: Yang, Goncu, Pantelous (2018), Int. Review of Financial Analysis 60, 177-196
evidence.quote: the intra-day strategies used cannot generate sufficiently enough high excess returns to cover the excessive costs due to the higher frequency of trading.
